intelligence.falsifier: A cycle certified repeatable while consuming a finite retry budget; authority expiry under time progression ignored; monotonic policy revisions assumed away; terminal-state transitions omitted from the model; scheduler sequence treated as requiring literal state equality; infinite-speed scheduling inside finite intervals; abstraction that drops a resource counter and invents a spurious self-loop; solver UNKNOWN/timeout promoted to proof; budget semantics invented (eligible-unserved rounds do not consume ACT retries); busy pools misread as ineligibility.

human_view.meaning: Finding a loop is the easy part — the hard part is proving the loop doesn't secretly run out of something. The state must be complete: not just 'the scheduler is at node q1' but the obligation identity, the LAW authorization and its expiry, the policy and incident revisions, the retry budget, the resource quota, the clock, whether the obligation is still alive, and what the evidence actually shows. Then four machine-checkable obligations: the entry reaches a state satisfying the invariant; every cycle traversal from any invariant state stays in the invariant; every traversal adds debt; and the exit stays reachable from every invariant state. The three false cycles teach the lesson: a loop consuming retry tokens dies when the tokens run out; a loop racing a two-second clock with 100ms rounds caps at 20; a loop under a mandatory policy change breaks when the old authorization expires. Only the fourth — pure waiting that consumes nothing, with valid authority and no finite limit — can genuinely repeat. The invariant handles legitimately changing values correctly: sequence numbers may increase, debt may grow, time may advance — what matters is whether the change can disable the next lap. The expiry-time example is the canonical trap: t<expiresAt looks fine until you notice t grows every iteration. Minimization comes only after proving relevance: for each variable, ask whether it can affect enabledness, repeatability, debt growth, exit validity, or observation compatibility — remove it only on five proven no's, and carry the abstraction proof with the witness. Twelve fixtures, crowned by the CONTROL/TREATMENT pair: identical models except one consumes retry tokens (must reject) and one doesn't (must accept) — proving the system understands operation semantics, not just graph shapes.

Encode the complete state; prove the four obligations by induction; contract every hidden constraint; distinguish stable/evolving/consumable variables; scrutinize infinite-speed abstractions; abstract only by proof-preserving reduction with the abstraction proof attached.
